messages.author: df56e4ef17f4bbd2
messages.subject: clarification request w.r.t. RSNNS/MLP - regression
parts:
Dear    Dr Christoph Bergmeir:


Further to our communication through LinkedIn, code and question appears below and related CSV files are attached herewith.

      #  fermentation ANN fitting using RSNNS /mlp

      library(RSNNS)

      ##  load  train data set which has 30 rows , make it matrix and scale it

      ferment <- read.csv('fermentative production of scleroglucan  by ANN.csv') 
      ferment_mat <- data.matrix(ferment)
       x <-    scale(ferment_mat[, 2:5], center = T) 
       y <-  data.matrix(ferment_mat[, 6:6])

## build model using all train data

fit_w_mlp <- mlp(x, y, size = 4,learnFuncParams=c(.1), maxit = 1000, initFunc = "Randomize_Weights",            learnFunc = "Std_Backpropagation",   updateFunc = "Topological_Order",            hiddenActFunc = "Act_Logistic",   shufflePatterns = TRUE,    linOut = T, inputsTest = NULL,targetsTest = NULL) 

 print(fit_w_mlp)

##  model fits the data well,  predict  function works well too 

 predicted  <-predict(x = x,  fit_w_mlp )

      cor( y,predicted)

##  load  unknown test dataset with 16 records , make it matrix, scale it

  ferment_test <- read.csv('fermentative production of scleroglucan  by ANN unseen.csv')         ferment_mat_test <- data.matrix(ferment_test)
 x_test <-    scale(ferment_mat_test[, 2:5], center = T) 
 y_test <-  data.matrix(ferment_mat_test[, 6:6])

## predict does not give error but shows  30 records ??

predicted_test  <-predict(x = x_test,  fit_w_mlp  )

##  as expected gives error: Error in cor(y_test, predicted_test) : incompatible ##   dimensions

cor( y_test,predicted_test)

 

Question is : why does the predict not work properly??

If model is re-built with unknown data it does work.
Could you please clarify why this problem is occuring?


Also could you please provide any writeup on MLP regression with complete list of options.

Thanks
Jagadish
--

messages.author: 47597751d567aea1
messages.subject: Re: clarification request w.r.t. RSNNS/MLP - regression
parts:
Dear Jagadish,

the problem is that the predict function (predict.rsnns) has a parameter called newdata, not x. Try with:

predicted_test <-predict(fit_w_mlp, newdata = x_test)

As to your question about documentation, between the package manual, the JSS paper, the original SNNS Manual, and maybe the report from Seymour Shlien, which is all referenced on page 5 of the package manual (https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/RSNNS/RSNNS.pdf), you should find your way.

Regards,
Christoph

messages.subject: Re: clarification request w.r.t. RSNNS/MLP - regression
parts:
Hi,

yes, one thing I noticed is that you normalize training and test set
independently. You should normalize the test set with the normalization
parameters (mean, sd) from the training set. RSNNS has a function
normTrainingAndTestSet to do that.

Regards,
Christoph

messages.subject: Re: clarification request w.r.t. RSNNS/MLP - regression
parts:
Hi,

an example is, e.g., the "iris" demo in the package:

https://github.com/cbergmeir/RSNNS/blob/master/RSNNS/demo/iris.R

If your model performs better in training than in testing this means
that you are overfitting. You should try using less hidden units then,
for example.

Regards,
Christoph
